newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH PM TO SET UP ANTI-BUREAUCRACY BUREAU - PAPER.
newsitem.headline: CZECH PM TO SET UP ANTI-BUREAUCRACY BUREAU - PAPER.

text.p: Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus will attack fabled Bohemian bureaucracy by setting up a state commission to collect complaints on state commissions, bureaus and ministries, the daily Mlada Fronta reported on Friday.
It quoted Klaus as saying his centre-right Civic Democratic Party would spearhead the body aimed at quelling citizens' disdain of arrogant bureaucrats and cutting red tape.

"(Bureaucratic proceedings) sometimes tend to be in apparent disparity of common sense with citizens and with their natural and legitimate demand for the smallest possible interference of offices into their lives," the independent daily quoted Klaus as saying at a party meeting.

An anti-bureaucracy bureau may be fitting for the home of the early 20th-century novelist Franz Kafka whose bureacratically-driven angst became part of literary lore in such stories as "The Trial" and "The Castle".

Although 40 years of Communism did little to keep the efficiency of state organisations sharp, Czech civil service payrolls have ballooned since post-Communist privatisation began after the 1989 revolution.
